goal: Give msfslogger a tracked pre-flight/ground session — starting the moment the aircraft is on the ground, stationary and engines off (freshly spawned at a gate or cold-and-dark) — so ACARS dispatch-release and loadsheet-request actions have real airport and parking-position context before pushback, not only after rotation. Automatic detection (new agent telemetry plus a new flightManager ground state) is the primary mechanism; manual airport/ramp entry is an explicit fallback for when detection cannot resolve a position, not an equal alternative.
frozen_decisions: src/flightManager.ts: state machine is IDLE -> FLYING only. From IDLE, a flight starts only after 3 consecutive frames of !frame.onGround && airspeedKnots > 30 (AIRBORNE_DEBOUNCE_FRAMES), not in slew. Landing requires onGround && groundSpeedKnots < 5 for 10 frames. No ground-speed/engine/parking-brake signal is used today, and no "parked at gate" state exists.

ACARS is NOT actually gated on a live flight record: src/acars.ts, src/routes/acars.ts, src/routes/plannedLegs.ts, src/db/acarsMessages.ts key dispatch release and loadsheet request off planned_leg_id alone (schema comment: "a dispatch release arrives before pushback, when no flights row has been created yet"). Loadsheet request is gated on dispatch data existing (409 NO_DISPATCH_DATA), not on flight state. The backend contract already tolerates pre-flight access — confirmed by investigation (see risks/summary): the user-visible gap is the client, which only ever reaches client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx via /flight/:id/acars, a flight-scoped route with no equivalent entry point for a planned leg that has no flights row yet. src/db/acarsMessages.ts's listAcarsMessagesForPlannedLeg() already exists and is currently unused by any route — built for exactly this, per its own comment.

agent/agent.js polls at 1 Hz: lat/lon, altitude, IAS, ground velocity, heading, vertical speed, SIM ON GROUND, IS SLEW ACTIVE, aircraft title, plus pause/crash/FlightLoaded events. It does NOT request PARKING BRAKE POSITION, GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:n, or any parking-spot/gate SimVar — these are additions to the existing data definition, not a new mechanism.
src/airports.ts already does ICAO/geo lookups (findNearestAirport) — reuse for resolving nearest airport to a ground position rather than inventing new lookup logic.

src/legMatcher.ts's matchPlannedLeg() is a pure function already used by flightManager.ts's autoLinkPlannedLeg() at takeoff, against the active trip's candidates within DEPARTURE_RADIUS_NM — reuse it unchanged for ground-state auto-linking rather than inventing a second matching algorithm.
Design step is NOT skipped: this run introduces a new flightManager state (a contract), a new agent->server telemetry field set, and likely a new/changed API surface for manual entry.

DevOps is an expected skip (no build/packaging/deploy surface anticipated) — confirmed by this Plan: grep of README.md for state-machine, SimVar, engine and brake language found nothing this run needs to update, and no dependency, build or packaging file is touched by any task below.

Never touch the user's running server (port 3000) or live flights.db — scratch port + copied DB only. Node 20 via nvm for every node/npm/npx/server command. Verification beyond Vitest is npx tsc / npm run build, curl against a scratch server, better-sqlite3 queries, and ts-node CLI inspectors.
sequencing_rationale: One Designer task (T-001) freezes the whole contract up front — state name and debounce rule, agent telemetry fields, the ground_sessions schema, the auto-link algorithm's reuse of matchPlannedLeg/findNearestAirport, the REST surface for manual entry and for leg-scoped ACARS, the client wire types, and the manual-vs-auto precedence rule — because all four later work-streams (agent, flightManager, routes, client) reference the same records and must agree before any of them writes code.

Phase 1 ships the escape hatch — manual airport/ramp entry, the ground_sessions table, and a leg-scoped ACARS thread the client can actually reach — before Phase 2 wires up the automatic detection that supersedes it, per the rule that a manual override ships before the automation it protects. It is also independently useful: it answers half of the user's original ask ("allow the user to manually send information on the airport and ramp/gate they're currently at") without touching agent.js or flightManager.ts at all.

Phase 2 adds the primary, automatic path: new agent telemetry (single-seam addition to an existing data definition, Jr, and independent of every other Phase 2 file) and the flightManager ground-state machine (Sr, cross-module but re-using existing geo/matching code rather than inventing it), then the client surfaces the auto-detected session and its precedence over the Phase 1 manual form.

Within each phase, the backend task's allowed_paths (src/**, agent/**, tests/**) and the frontend task's (client/src/**) are disjoint, and both depend only on the phase's design freeze (or the prior phase's reviewer) rather than on each other, so they may run in parallel; Phase 2's agent.js task and its flightManager task are likewise mutually independent files.

Every phase ends in a reviewer task, and the first task of the next phase depends on it — this is what stops a Phase 2 edit to src/server.ts/src/types.ts from ever running concurrently with Phase 1's still-unreviewed edits to those same files.

The frontend task in Phase 2 depends on the Phase 2 backend task (not just the design freeze) because its acceptance criteria require curling a live /api/status field that only that task adds — unlike Phase 1, where backend and frontend can genuinely run in parallel against the frozen contract alone.

phases.name: Escape hatch: manual ground entry, ground-session persistence, leg-scoped ACARS reachability
phases.ships: A pilot who has just spawned at a gate can tell msfslogger which airport and ramp/gate they're at; that creates a ground session the app remembers, and from it (or from any unflown planned leg in a trip) the user can now reach the ACARS thread and send dispatch/loadsheet/canned/WX actions before pushback — a capability that today is only reachable after takeoff.

phases.name: Automatic ground-state detection
phases.ships: From the moment MSFS loads a flight on the ground, stationary, engines off — no user action required — msfslogger detects it, resolves the airport (and planned leg, if one matches) automatically, and the ACARS actions from Phase 1 light up on their own; the Phase 1 manual form remains as the labeled fallback for when detection doesn't fire or gets it wrong.

tasks.title: Freeze the ground-state contract: telemetry, schema, matching, REST surface, client wire types, manual/auto precedence
tasks.goal: Write .claude/runs/2026-09-15-preflight-ground-tracking/design.md with these numbered sections, in this order, so every later task can cite one by number: (1) the new flightManager state — its name, entry condition (on-ground, ~zero groundspeed, engines off and/or parking brake set) and a debounce constant mirroring AIRBORNE_DEBOUNCE_FRAMES/LANDED_DEBOUNCE_FRAMES, plus every transition in and out of it (including from onCrash()/onSimDisconnect(), which today only handle FLYING); (2) the agent -> server telemetry contract — exact SimVar names (e.g. PARKING BRAKE POSITION, GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1..n) and read order to append to agent/agent.js's DEF_FLIGHT_DATA, the exact new SimFrame field names, and the isValidFrame() validation change in src/ingest.ts; (3) the ground_sessions table DDL (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, in the style already in src/db/schema.ts) — columns for airport icao/name, lat/lon, parking/ramp position (nullable), source ('auto'|'manual'), planned_leg_id (nullable FK), started_at/ended_at, and any ALTER TABLE additions needed elsewhere, each guarded by the existing PRAGMA table_info idiom; (4) the auto-detection/auto-link algorithm — confirms reuse of findNearestAirport (src/airports.ts) and matchPlannedLeg (src/legMatcher.ts, same DEPARTURE_RADIUS_NM candidates as autoLinkPlannedLeg) rather than new geo logic, and specifies a pure module (e.g. src/groundState.ts) holding the debounce/entry decision, isolated the same way src/legMatcher.ts is, with a named CLI inspector (e.g. src/inspect-groundstate.ts) mirroring src/inspect-legmatch.ts's harness style; (5) the REST surface — method/path/body/response for a manual-entry endpoint, a current-ground-session read (and how it folds into GET /api/status, following the existing conditional-spread idiom for plannedLeg/traffic in src/server.ts), and new leg-scoped ACARS thread routes (GET and POST, canned + wx) mirroring the flight-scoped ones in src/routes/acars.ts but keyed on planned_leg_id and reusing the already-present-but-unused listAcarsMessagesForPlannedLeg (src/db/acarsMessages.ts); (6) the client contract — the wire types to mirror byte-for-byte into client/src/types.ts, and where in the client the ground session and the leg-scoped ACARS thread become reachable (a new route, and a link from the trip page's planned-leg rows); (7) the manual-vs-auto precedence rule — what happens when both exist for the same session/leg, whether an auto-detected session may overwrite a manual one, and the exact wording the client must use to present manual entry as fallback, not an equal alternative.
acceptance_criteria: design.md exists with exactly the 7 numbered sections above, in order, and ctx.sh design 2026-09-15-preflight-ground-tracking <n> returns each in isolation.
Section 1 names the new FlightState value and states every transition into and out of it, including the onCrash()/onSimDisconnect() paths flightManager.ts currently only handles for FLYING.

Section 2 lists exact SimVar strings, units and SimConnect data types in the read order they must be added to DEF_FLIGHT_DATA, and the exact new SimFrame field names — no ambiguity left for the Jr agent task to resolve.
Section 3's DDL can be pasted verbatim into src/db/schema.ts's initDb() and is guarded the same way every other CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS there is.
Section 4 explicitly states that no new geo-matching algorithm is invented: findNearestAirport and matchPlannedLeg are reused as-is, with only the calling code being new.

Section 5 gives a concrete path, method and JSON shape for every new endpoint, and states the exact key(s) added to GET /api/status's response, present iff the ground state is active (never a literal null).
Section 6 lists every new/changed client/src/types.ts interface by name and field, and names the exact page(s)/route(s) that become reachable.
Section 7 states, in one sentence a reviewer can check against the client code, how manual entry is labeled as fallback.
No implementation code beyond interface stubs/DDL text inside design.md or contracts/.
